The Central Bank of Nigeria has granted final approval to Milestone Global Bank Limited to operate as a regional non-interest bank, following the institution’s compliance with regulatory requirements on capital, governance and non-interest banking operations. The approval clears the way for the bank to enter Nigeria’s financial services industry, with plans to offer digital banking services and establish physical branches in Abuja, Kano and Kaduna. This was disclosed in a statement issued by the bank on Tuesday, which indicated that the institution was completing the remaining operational arrangements ahead of its official commencement of business. “Milestone Global Bank Limited has announced the receipt of its final approval as a regional non-interest bank from the Central Bank of Nigeria, marking a significant milestone in the Bank’s institutional journey and paving the way for its entry into Nigeria’s financial services sector,” the statement read. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Milestone Global Bank, AbdulFattah Amoo, described the approval as a major development in the bank’s efforts to establish itself in Nigeria’s financial sector. It signals our readiness to serve everyday customers, enterprises, corporates, and government agencies as we move towards the commencement of operations.” According to the statement, the bank intends to provide ethical financial services supported by digital technology, data and automation, targeting individuals, businesses and government institutions. Amoo explained that the institution would focus on combining non-interest banking principles with modern financial services to improve accessibility and customer experience. “Our vision is to be the preferred ethical financial institution in Africa, combining ethical financial principles with modern banking capabilities, strong governance and a genuine commitment to enabling prosperity,” he said. He added, “We will open our doors as a bank Nigerians can rely on, leveraging technology, data and automation to improve service delivery, efficiency and accessibility for the customers and communities we serve.” The bank disclosed that its services would initially be available through digital channels and physical locations in Abuja, Kano and Kaduna, with plans for subsequent expansion to other parts of the country. The development comes amid efforts by the CBN to deepen financial inclusion and expand alternative financing options in Nigeria’s banking industry. Non-interest banking is a financial model that prohibits conventional interest-based transactions and instead relies on arrangements such as profit-sharing, leasing and asset-backed financing. The sector includes institutions such as Jaiz Bank, TAJBank, Lotus Bank, The Alternative Bank and Summit Bank, which have received regulatory authorisation to operate in the non-interest banking segment. With Milestone Global Bank’s approval, the number of authorised non-interest banks is expected to increase, although the institution has yet to announce the commencement of commercial operations. Under the CBN’s revised minimum capital requirements announced in March 2024, regional non-interest banks are required to maintain a minimum capital base of N10bn, while national non-interest banks must meet a N20bn threshold.
